nodes.role: Charles Lee Powell Chair in Wireless Communications, UC San Diego
nodes.name: Robert Heath
nodes.description: Leading voice on MIMO and extreme MIMO for 6G. Joined UC San Diego in 2024 from NC State (and UT Austin before that). Panellist on the Next G Alliance's extreme MIMO panel (Jan 2026).

nodes.role: Professor, EE, University of Notre Dame; Policy Outreach Director, SpectrumX
nodes.name: Monisha Ghosh
nodes.description: Former FCC Chief Technology Officer (to June 2021) and SpectrumX Policy Outreach Director. Argues 6G should be 'sharing native'. Testified to the Senate Commerce Committee on spectrum and national security (March 2024). Co-chairs the FCC TAC Advanced Spectrum Sharing working group.

nodes.role: Director, SpectrumX; Professor, University of Notre Dame
nodes.name: Nick Laneman
nodes.description: Director of SpectrumX, the NSF Spectrum Innovation Center led by Notre Dame.

nodes.role: SVP Engineering, Qualcomm Technologies
nodes.name: John Smee
nodes.description: Runs Qualcomm's 6G strategy. Has said pre-commercial 6G trials target the LA 2028 Olympics, with commercial rollout from late 2029.

nodes.role: 6G research lead, Qualcomm
nodes.name: Tingfang Ji
nodes.description: Described as Qualcomm's 6G research leader. Co-author of '6G Takes Shape' with Jeff Andrews and Todd Humphreys.

nodes.role: Nokia Fellow, Nokia Standards and Strategy; Chair, Next G Alliance Technology Roadmap Working Group
nodes.name: Amitava Ghosh
nodes.description: Nokia Fellow and Head of Radio Interface Group. Chairs the Next G Alliance Technology Roadmap Working Group (previously the National 6G Roadmap Working Group). Based at Nokia in Naperville, IL.

nodes.role: Former President, Bell Labs Core Research, Nokia (retired July 2026)
nodes.name: Peter Vetter
nodes.description: Led Bell Labs Core Research for nearly two decades, latterly as co-president of Bell Labs. Retired on 17 July 2026 when Nokia merged its two research units under new head Guru Parulkar, amid cuts and the move from Murray Hill to New Brunswick, NJ.

nodes.role: AT&T Fellow; AVP Wireless Technology & Standards, AT&T
nodes.name: Brian Daly
nodes.description: AT&T Fellow who leads AT&T's standards strategy. Co-chair of the FCC TAC 6G Working Group, co-chair of the Next G Alliance Steering Group, and co-lead of the National Spectrum Consortium 5G/Next G Working Group.

nodes.name: 3GPP
nodes.description: The global partnership that writes mobile standards (LTE, 5G NR and now 6G). Its plenaries include TSG RAN (radio) and TSG SA (system architecture). Support centre hosted by ETSI in Sophia Antipolis, France.

nodes.name: ITU-R Working Party 5D
nodes.description: The UN ITU group responsible for IMT standards, including IMT-2030 (6G). Sets the 6G requirements and evaluates candidate technologies such as 3GPP's.

nodes.name: ITU-APT Foundation of India (IAFI)
nodes.description: Non-profit Indian industry foundation and ITU sector member. Its President, Bharat Bhatia, chairs ITU-R WP 5D's Working Group on General Aspects for IMT-2030 (6G).

nodes.name: University of Surrey 6G Innovation Centre (6GIC)
nodes.description: The UK's first 6G Innovation Centre, within Surrey's Institute for Communication Systems (also home of the world's first 5G centre, 5GIC). Partners with InterDigital on 6G research and led the £12M government-funded TUDOR project.

nodes.name: Samsung R&D Institute UK
nodes.description: Samsung's UK research centre, part of Samsung's global 6G research programme.

nodes.name: Ericsson UK 6G research programme
nodes.description: Ericsson's UK-based 6G research programme, launched in 2022 with a ten-year, tens-of-millions-of-pounds commitment and renewed in June 2025. Worked on the UK government-backed REASON and TUDOR projects.

nodes.name: TUDOR
nodes.description: Towards Ubiquitous 3D Open Resilient Network: a £12M DSIT-funded UK flagship 6G research project (Feb 2023 to Jan 2025) led by Surrey's 6GIC, integrating satellite, airborne and terrestrial networks. Consortium included Ericsson, InterDigital, BT, BAE Systems and Qualcomm.

nodes.name: REASON
nodes.description: Realising Enabling Architectures and Solutions for Open Networks: UK government-backed project developing a roadmap for open 6G networks. Includes Ericsson, Samsung and Nokia.

nodes.name: University of Oulu / 6G Flagship
nodes.description: Finnish university running 6G Flagship, the world's first large-scale 6G research programme (from 2018). Also runs NATO DIANA's 6G test centre.

nodes.name: Khalifa University 6G Research Center
nodes.description: 6G Research Center at Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi, led by Merouane Debbah. Built TelecomGPT, a telco-first large language model, and works with GSMA Foundry on open telecom AI models and benchmarks.

nodes.name: 6G Forum (Korea)
nodes.description: Korea's national 6G industry and research forum. Has run joint workshops with the Next G Alliance.

nodes.name: 6G Smart Networks and Services Industry Association (6G-IA)
nodes.description: European industry association for 6G; the private-side partner of the EU's Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking (SNS JU).

nodes.name: Bharat 6G Alliance
nodes.description: India's 6G alliance of industry, operators, academia and research institutions, launched by the Department of Telecommunications in July 2023. Grown to about 90 members with seven working groups. India targets at least 10% of global 6G patents and standards.

nodes.name: IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group (China)
nodes.description: China's government-backed 6G promotion group coordinating research, standards and international cooperation on IMT-2030 (6G).

nodes.name: XG Mobile Promotion Forum (XGMF)
nodes.description: Japan's forum promoting 5G evolution and 6G (Beyond 5G) research, standards and deployment.

nodes.name: NGMN Alliance
nodes.description: Global operator-led alliance (Next Generation Mobile Networks) that sets operator requirements and priorities for each generation, including 6G.

nodes.name: Huawei
nodes.description: Chinese telecoms vendor and a major player in 6G research and standards.

nodes.role: Head of Cellular Standard, HWT Department, Apple
nodes.name: Wanshi Chen
nodes.description: Leads cellular standards at Apple. Formerly at Qualcomm (from 2006), where he was 3GPP TSG RAN Plenary Chair (April 2021 to January 2025, the most senior radio role in 3GPP), RAN1 Chair (2017 to 2021) and RAN1 Vice Chair (2013 to 2017), leading delivery of the first 5G NR releases. Lead Editor of IEEE Communications Magazine's Mobile Communications and Network Series.

nodes.role: Master (VP of Technology), Samsung Research; 3GPP TSG RAN Chair
nodes.name: Younsun Kim
nodes.description: Current 3GPP TSG RAN Chair (elected March 2025, term to March 2027) and the first Korean in the role. Samsung Research Master; previously chaired RAN WG1 (2021–2025). Succeeded Wanshi Chen.

nodes.role: Senior Principal Engineer & Senior Director of Standards, Intel; 3GPP TSG SA Chair
nodes.name: Puneet Jain
nodes.description: 3GPP TSG SA (Service and System Aspects) Plenary Chair since 2023, re-elected for a second term in March 2025. Previously chaired SA WG2.

nodes.role: Samsung Research; Chair, ITU-R Coordination Group on IMT-2030 (6G)
nodes.name: HyoungJin Choi
nodes.description: Samsung Research researcher named chair of ITU-R WP 5D's Coordination Group on IMT-2030 (6G) in July 2024, serving until 2029. Previously chaired the ITU-R 6G Vision Group (2021–2023).

nodes.role: President, IAFI; Chair, ITU-R WP 5D Working Group on General Aspects
nodes.name: Bharat Bhatia
nodes.description: President of the ITU-APT Foundation of India and Vice Chairman of the Wireless World Research Forum. Chairs ITU-R WP 5D's Working Group on General Aspects, which develops IMT-2030 (6G) documents including the call for candidate technologies.

nodes.role: Regius Professor; Founding Director, 5GIC, 6GIC and Institute for Communication Systems, University of Surrey
nodes.name: Rahim Tafazolli
nodes.description: Regius Professor of Electronic Engineering at Surrey and founder and director of the Institute for Communication Systems, the 5G Innovation Centre and the 6G Innovation Centre (the UK's first). Led the £12M TUDOR project and set up a 6G research partnership with InterDigital.

nodes.role: Vice Rector for Research, University of Oulu; former Director, 6G Flagship
nodes.name: Matti Latva-aho
nodes.description: Led Finland's 6G Flagship from its start in 2018 until mid-2025. Vice Rector for Research at the University of Oulu since July 2025 (term to 2030). IEEE Fellow.

nodes.role: Director, 6G Flagship, University of Oulu
nodes.name: Ari Pouttu
nodes.description: Director of 6G Flagship since 2025, succeeding Matti Latva-aho (previously Vice-Director).

nodes.role: Director of Sustainability and Regulation, 6G Flagship
nodes.name: Marja Matinmikko-Blue
nodes.description: Director of Sustainability and Regulation at 6G Flagship, University of Oulu; works on the path from 6G research to spectrum regulation.

nodes.role: Senior Expert, Radio Access, Ericsson
nodes.name: Erik Dahlman
nodes.description: One of the most influential architects of the LTE and 5G standards, now leading Ericsson's 6G standardisation work with Stefan Parkvall. Keynote at the 6G@UT Forum 2025.

nodes.role: Senior Expert, Cellular Radio Access, Ericsson
nodes.name: Stefan Parkvall
nodes.description: One of the most influential architects of the LTE and 5G standards, now leading Ericsson's 6G standardisation work with Erik Dahlman. Keynote at the 6G@UT Forum 2025.

nodes.role: Director, 6G Research Center, Khalifa University
nodes.name: Merouane Debbah
nodes.description: Founding director of Khalifa University's 6G Research Center. Leads TelecomGPT, a telco-first large language model, and the GSMA Foundry collaboration on open telecom AI. A key name where AI and 6G meet.

nodes.role: Executive Vice President, Samsung Research America; Head of Samsung Research 6G Team
nodes.name: Charlie Zhang
nodes.description: SVP at Samsung Research America and head of Samsung Research's 6G team, which publishes Samsung's 6G white papers. Vice Chair of the Next G Alliance Full Member Group. Former 3GPP RAN WG1 vice chair. IEEE Fellow. Quoted as Samsung Executive Vice President on the July 2026 Verizon ISAC trial in Dallas.

nodes.role: EVP and Head, Advanced Communications Research Center (ACRC), Samsung Research
nodes.name: JinGuk Jeong
nodes.description: Heads Samsung Research's Advanced Communications Research Center, leading research on AI-native networks and ISAC. Signed 6G MOUs with SK Telecom (AI-RAN, 2025) and LG Uplus (ISAC, 2026), and leads partnerships such as the Verizon 6G Innovation Forum.

nodes.role: Founding Chair, Bharat 6G Alliance; Chairman, Tejas Networks
nodes.name: N. G. Subramaniam
nodes.description: Founding chair of the Bharat 6G Alliance. Chairman of Tejas Networks and former COO of TCS.

nodes.name: Younghan Nam
nodes.role: Senior Director, Standards and Mobility Innovation Team, Samsung Research America
nodes.description: Senior Director in Samsung Research America's Standards and Mobility Innovation Team, where he leads 6G cellular system research. Earlier led 3GPP RAN1 work on mmWave, massive MIMO and 5G channel modelling. Works in Charlie Zhang's team. Speaker at the Next G Alliance and 6G Forum Korea joint workshop.

nodes.name: Vodafone Group
nodes.description: Global mobile operator. Its Group R&D team, led by Luke Ibbetson, shapes Vodafone's thinking on 6G, non-terrestrial networks and quantum. Separate from VodafoneThree, its UK joint venture.

nodes.name: Luke Ibbetson
nodes.role: Head of Group R&D, Vodafone Group; Board Director, NGMN
nodes.description: Head of Group R&D at Vodafone, with the company since 1996. Shapes Vodafone's thinking on 6G, non-terrestrial networks and quantum; pioneer of NB-IoT. Board director of the NGMN Alliance. Argues operators should deploy 6G when the technology is mature and in step with network refresh cycles. Named on the UK REASON project.

nodes.name: Christian Fager
nodes.role: Professor of Microwave Electronics, Chalmers University of Technology
nodes.description: Professor of Microwave Electronics at Chalmers and a project leader on the three-year Chalmers–Virginia Tech project on energy-efficient 6G radio, funded by the Swedish Research Council and NSF (VINES). Works on moving signal processing from the radio into the fibre network to cut energy losses.

nodes.name: Lars Svensson
nodes.role: Associate Professor of VLSI Systems, Chalmers University of Technology
nodes.description: Associate Professor of VLSI Systems at Chalmers, on the three-year Chalmers–Virginia Tech project on energy-efficient 6G radio funded by the Swedish Research Council and NSF (VINES).

nodes.name: Virginia Diodes (VDI)
nodes.address: 979 Second Street SE, Suite 309, Charlottesville, VA 22902
nodes.description: Makes millimetre-wave and terahertz test and measurement equipment and components (50 GHz to 2 THz), including network analyser, spectrum analyser and signal generator extension modules, built on in-house GaAs Schottky diodes. Relevant to sub-THz 6G research. Founded in 1996 as a University of Virginia spin-off; about 100 staff.

nodes.name: Thomas W. Crowe
nodes.role: CEO and Founder, Virginia Diodes (VDI)
nodes.description: CEO and founder of Virginia Diodes, the Charlottesville terahertz component and test equipment maker spun out of the University of Virginia in 1996.

nodes.name: Gerhard Schoenthal
nodes.role: Chief Operating Officer, Virginia Diodes (VDI)
nodes.description: Chief Operating Officer of Virginia Diodes, with the company since 2004. Speaks on terahertz technology for 6G, including at the 2020 6G Symposium. Physics PhD from the University of Virginia; former US Navy officer and Intel process engineer.

nodes.name: Nishith D. Tripathi
nodes.role: Research Associate Professor, ECE, Virginia Tech
nodes.description: Research associate professor in electrical and computer engineering at Virginia Tech. Principal investigator, with Jeff Reed as co-PI, on 'Securing Non-Terrestrial Networks in NextG', a 2021 Commonwealth Cyber Initiative project on security risks in satellite and air-to-ground networks for 6G.

nodes.name: ANSER (Analytic Services Inc.)
nodes.description: Not-for-profit public-service research institute supporting national and homeland security through independent analysis and practical solutions. Founded in 1958 as an Air Force federal contract research centre. Has a wireless communications policy practice covering 5G, ISAC, Open RAN, AI-RAN, spectrum management and satellite networking.

nodes.name: Department of War Office of the CIO
nodes.description: Office of the Department of War (Defense Department) Chief Information Officer, principal adviser to the Secretary of War on IT, cybersecurity, communications and spectrum. Leads the DoW 5G/6G enterprise strategy and 5G reference architecture for military installations; oversees DISA.

nodes.role: Chief Information Officer, Department of War
nodes.name: Kirsten Davies
nodes.description: Department of War CIO, sworn in on 23 December 2025 after Senate confirmation. Principal adviser to the Secretary of War on IT, cybersecurity and information assurance; oversees DISA. Her office runs the DoW 5G/6G enterprise strategy. Previously CISO at Unilever.

nodes.name: Ofinno
nodes.description: Research and development lab that invents and patents wireless and video technologies for 5G/6G, next-gen Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) and video compression standards. Its 6G work sits in a dedicated 6G Innovation Lab in Reston, with 3GPP delegates mainly in RAN1 and RAN2. Founded in 2011 by Esmael Dinan. Named a LexisNexis Top 100 Global Innovator for the fifth year running in 2026.

nodes.role: CEO, Ofinno
nodes.name: Kavon Nasabzadeh
nodes.description: CEO of Ofinno, the Reston R&D and patent lab working on 5G/6G, next-gen Wi-Fi and media compression standards.

nodes.name: Ali Cagatay Cirik
nodes.role: Technical Director, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Technical Director for 5G and 6G at Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab in Reston, at Ofinno since 2017. Works on 5G NR and MIMO signal processing. Previously at Sierra Wireless and a research fellow at the University of Oulu, Edinburgh and UBC. PhD, UC Riverside.

nodes.name: Taehun Kim
nodes.role: Senior Research Manager, Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Leads research on 5G and 6G radio access network procedures at Ofinno. Formerly chief research engineer for standardisation at LG Electronics, a 3GPP CT1 and RAN2 delegate, and rapporteur for a V2X work item. PhD, KAIST; postdoc at UCLA.

nodes.name: Yunjung Yi
nodes.role: Senior Manager, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Researches radio access technologies for LTE, NR and 6G at Ofinno. 3GPP delegate since 2011, working on LTE MTC, NB-IoT, 5G control channel and initial access, URLLC, SBFD and power saving. PhD, UCLA.

nodes.name: HyoungSuk Jeon
nodes.role: Senior Manager, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Senior Manager and Senior Principal Engineer in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, Reston.

nodes.name: Sechang Myung
nodes.role: Senior Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 researcher in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, working on network energy saving, initial access, and high-frequency and unlicensed spectrum.

nodes.name: Chiou-Wei (Joanne) Tsai
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 delegate and inventor in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, working on 6G control channel design, scheduling and HARQ. RAN1 delegate since 2017; Feature Lead for Rel-20 6GR Bandwidth Operation. Formerly at MediaTek.

nodes.name: Umut Ugurlu
nodes.role: Senior Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP delegate at Ofinno working on MIMO, beam management, HARQ, initial access, and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC).

nodes.name: Javad Abdoli
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Inventor at Ofinno focused on the 6G air interface. Formerly a 3GPP RAN1 delegate at Huawei and Intel, and a systems engineer at Mavenir and Samsung Research America. Named on 45+ US patents. PhD, University of Waterloo.

nodes.name: Jae-Nam Shim
nodes.role: Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 delegate at Ofinno working on 5G/6G wireless communications. Formerly in the standards division at LG Electronics.

nodes.name: Hyunsu Cha
nodes.role: Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Research engineer at Ofinno working on 6G initial access, MIMO, positioning, ISAC, Ambient IoT and AI/ML for wireless. 3GPP RAN1 delegate since 2017. Formerly senior staff engineer for 5G/6G research at Nokia Standards. PhD, Yonsei University.

nodes.name: Govind Ravikumar Gopal
nodes.role: Senior Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Works on AI/ML for 5G/6G channel state information (CSI) in 3GPP RAN1 at Ofinno. Formerly led 6G radio research in Nokia's Technology Standards group.

nodes.name: Jaehoon Chung
nodes.role: 3GPP Standards Engineer (RAN1), Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 standards engineer at Ofinno working on AI/ML-based CSI compression, beam management and MIMO.

nodes.name: Bighnaraj Panigrahi
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 5G-Advanced and 6G research and standardisation at Ofinno (3GPP RAN2). Formerly at Nokia and TCS.

nodes.name: Heng-Li (Henry) Chin
nodes.role: Senior Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Layer 2 protocol specialist and inventor at Ofinno (3GPP RAN2), with 90+ patents. Formerly at MediaTek.

nodes.name: Joondoo Kim
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 6G standards research engineer at Ofinno focused on 3GPP RAN2 user plane. Spent 14 years at Samsung Electronics as a network system architect on MAC scheduling for 4G/5G base stations. PhD, Yonsei University.

nodes.name: GyeongCheol Lee
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Specialist in 3GPP RAN2 user plane protocols at Ofinno, with 10+ years on LTE, NR and 6G. Formerly RAN2 UP Manager at LG Electronics.

nodes.name: Marta Martinez Tarradell
nodes.role: Principal Engineer, 3GPP Standards, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN2 delegate at Ofinno working on 4G/5G/6G wireless standardisation.

nodes.name: Jaewook Lee
nodes.role: Senior Staff Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN2 contributor at Ofinno, in RAN2 since 2009. Previously worked on LTE and NR standards at LG Electronics and on network systemisation at Ericsson LG.

nodes.name: Tiep Hoang
nodes.role: Patent Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Patent engineer at Ofinno with a research background in physical layer security, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and AI/ML optimisation for wireless. Postdoc at RIT, CU Denver and Southampton. PhD, Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.name: Aloizio P. Da Silva
nodes.role: Director, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Director of the CCI xG Testbed in Arlington since 2020, leading a team of faculty, postdocs, graduate research assistants and interns. Works on wireless networking (NFV, SDN, SDR), radio access and core networks, and large-scale testbed experimentation. Also research faculty in Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE. Previously with the NSF PAWR programme. Not related to CCI executive director Luiz DaSilva.

nodes.name: Joao Santos
nodes.role: Research Assistant Professor; 5G Testbed and AI Assurance Researcher, CCI
nodes.description: CCI research assistant professor working on radio resource management, radio virtualisation, network slicing, network security and end-to-end orchestration. PI on an NSF CISE CORE grant (about $553k, three years) on natively resilient 6G networks.

nodes.name: Sayanta Seth
nodes.role: Postdoctoral Associate, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Postdoctoral associate on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN, digital twins, AI-native wireless, FR3/mmWave spectrum coexistence, 6G and cislunar communications, plus commercial O-RAN interoperability and security testing. Formerly a postdoc at NC State's NextG Wireless Lab. PhD, University of Central Florida.

nodes.name: WiSig Networks
nodes.address: Academic Block-C, IIT Hyderabad, Kandi, Sangareddy, Telangana 502285, India
nodes.description: Indian 5G and O-RAN equipment, software and services company (O-CU, O-DU, O-RU, SMO, massive MIMO radios), incubated at IIT Hyderabad and founded in 2016 by Prof Kiran Kuchi. Testing its O-RAN components at the CCI xG Testbed OTIC for global commercialisation.

nodes.name: DISH Wireless (EchoStar)
nodes.description: EchoStar subsidiary that built the first US standalone Open RAN 5G network and co-hosted the North American O-RAN OTIC at CCI. After EchoStar sold spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX in 2025, Dish began decommissioning its Open RAN network; Dish Wireless filed for bankruptcy in 2026. Ran the NTIA-funded ORCID Open RAN test centre in Cheyenne, WY.

nodes.name: Jacek Kibilda
nodes.role: Research Associate Professor, CCI and Virginia Tech ECE
nodes.description: Research associate professor at CCI and Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE, and associate research faculty on the xG Testbed. Models and designs NextG mobile networks using stochastic geometry, AI and optimisation. Formerly a research fellow at CONNECT, Trinity College Dublin.

nodes.name: Madhura Adeppady
nodes.role: Postdoctoral Researcher, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Postdoctoral researcher on the CCI xG Testbed working on resource-efficient orchestration of microservices in edge computing, interference-aware placement and serverless systems.

nodes.name: Zeeshan Shah
nodes.role: Principal Engineer, Verizon 5G O-RAN Lab; resident engineer at CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Verizon principal engineer based at the CCI xG Testbed as a resident engineer, working on 5G O-RAN ACCoRD testing and integration.

nodes.name: Md. Habibur Rahman
nodes.role: PhD student and graduate research assistant, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Virginia Tech electrical engineering PhD student and CCI graduate research assistant on the xG Testbed, working on machine learning for wireless networks and O-RAN.

nodes.name: Asheesh Tripathi
nodes.role: PhD student and graduate research assistant, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Virginia Tech PhD student and CCI graduate research assistant working on spectrum sharing, ML in wireless systems, O-RAN and the SDR-based CBRS testbed at Stroubles Creek. Co-author of the testbed's 2025 IEEE Communications Magazine paper.

nodes.name: Mahesha Vidurange
nodes.role: PhD student, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN security and interoperability and AI/ML-based management.

nodes.name: Ishtiaque Ahmed
nodes.role: PhD student, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on cloud solutions for O-RAN and ACCoRD interoperability testing.

nodes.name: Manikantha Rayudu
nodes.role: PhD student, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on federated learning for IoT, extending to O-RAN.

nodes.name: Atif Ahmed
nodes.role: Research Intern, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Research intern on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN Open Fronthaul testing for ACCoRD.

nodes.name: Harshit Sai Teja Doddi
nodes.role: Master's Researcher / Intern, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Master's researcher and intern on the CCI xG Testbed admin team, handling network administration and management.

nodes.name: Kiran Kuchi
nodes.role: Founder, WiSig Networks; Professor, IIT Hyderabad
nodes.description: Founder of WiSig Networks and professor of electrical engineering at IIT Hyderabad. Contributor to 3GPP 5G/6G standards and works with the Indian government on its 6G roadmap. Leading WiSig's O-RAN testing with the CCI xG Testbed.

nodes.name: Abside Networks
nodes.description: US designer and manufacturer of 4G/5G and O-RAN radio systems, including massive MIMO units and private 5G SA systems for federal spectrum (n79). xG Testbed partner at CCI and a RAPID ISAC awardee with Northeastern University.

nodes.name: Altio Labs
nodes.description: R&D firm adapting 3GPP cellular technology for DoD uses: telemetry, positioning and sensing. RAPID ISAC awardee with Arizona State, DASH Tech IC and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: Arizona State University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC team member with Altio Labs, DASH Tech IC and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: DASH Tech Integrated Circuits
nodes.description: SoC design firm spun out of Arizona State and the University of Michigan in 2021. Builds domain-adaptive processors for RF sensing and communications at the edge, for commercial and DoD use. RAPID ISAC team member.

nodes.name: Mississippi State University
nodes.description: Public research university. On two RAPID ISAC teams: with Altio Labs, ASU and DASH Tech IC, and on the INSPIRED ISAC platform with NC State and the University of Utah.

nodes.name: Michigan State University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC awardee with George Mason University; also leads an NTIA-funded AI-driven O-RAN testing project with GMU.

nodes.name: Leidos
nodes.description: Defence, IT and science integrator. RAPID ISAC awardee with Tiami Networks.

nodes.name: University of Utah
nodes.description: Public research university and home of the POWDER PAWR wireless testbed. On the RAPID INSPIRED ISAC platform team ($3M) with NC State and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: System & Technology Research (STR)
nodes.description: Defence R&D company. RAPID ISAC awardee with Northeastern University.

nodes.name: Texas A&M University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC team member with UC San Diego, IBM and Northrop Grumman. Academic partner on the CCI xG Testbed project.

nodes.name: IBM
nodes.description: Technology company. RAPID ISAC team member with Texas A&M, UC San Diego and Northrop Grumman.

nodes.name: ANDRO Computational Solutions
nodes.description: Defence and commercial R&D firm working on software-defined waveforms, AI for RF spectrum sensing and wireless networking. RAPID ISAC team member with Parallel Wireless and Virginia Tech.

nodes.name: Salvador D'Itri
nodes.role: Chair, National Spectrum Consortium
nodes.description: Chair of the National Spectrum Consortium, which oversees a 350+ member ecosystem and the OTA contracting vehicle for DoW next-generation wireless prototypes. Long-time Federated Wireless executive (VP Federal) and former Wireless Innovation Forum board member. Previously chaired NSC 2019 to 2021.

nodes.name: David Kirkwood
nodes.role: Program Manager, OCUDU, FutureG Office, OUSW(R&E)
nodes.description: Program Manager for the FutureG Office's OCUDU programme. Building the public-private partnership behind OCUDU with the Linux Foundation and the National Spectrum Consortium, including the OCUDU Ecosystem Foundation (68+ members).

nodes.name: Deutsche Telekom
nodes.description: German telecoms group and majority owner of T-Mobile US. Its Group Technology unit runs network strategy, architecture, standardisation and patents, and is steering the group towards AI-native networks and 6G. Long-standing NGMN Alliance board member.

nodes.name: Arash Ashouriha
nodes.role: SVP Group Technology, Deutsche Telekom
nodes.description: Leads Group Technology at Deutsche Telekom: technology strategy, network evolution, architecture, standardisation, patents and innovation, including the move to AI-native networks and 6G. Previously headed Group Technology Architecture & Innovation, steering DT's 5G work. Chaired the NGMN Alliance Board 2020 to 2025. Joined DT in 2016 after 15 years at Vodafone Group, latterly Chief Network Officer for Germany & Central Europe.

nodes.name: Networks and Systems Security Lab (NSSL), Virginia Tech
nodes.description: Virginia Tech security lab led by Professors Angelos Stavrou and Haining Wang. Work spans NextG and 5G/6G security, cellular and wireless network security, Zero Trust and Named Data Networking for 6G, post-quantum cryptography for 5G, and AI security.

nodes.name: Quokka (formerly Kryptowire)
nodes.address: 3031 Tisch Way, Suite 505, San Jose, CA 95128

nodes.name: Ericsson Ottawa R&D site
nodes.address: 349 Terry Fox Drive, Kanata, Ottawa, ON K2K 2V6, Canada
nodes.description: Ericsson's largest R&D site in North America (about 1,700 staff), in the Kanata North tech park. End-to-end development and verification centre, home of the Ottawa Open Lab for Cloud RAN, and now focused on 6G and autonomous networks. Site lead: Tania Leppert (from 2026, succeeding Marcos Cavaletti).

nodes.name: Ericsson Montreal R&D centre and AI Hub
nodes.address: 8275 route Transcanadienne, Saint-Laurent, QC H4S 0B6, Canada
nodes.description: Ericsson's Montreal R&D and services centre (1,000+ staff) and home of its Global AI Accelerator, now the Ericsson AI Hub Canada. Works on AI-powered network management, quantum communications, Cloud RAN, 5G Advanced and 6G.

nodes.name: Ericsson Canada
nodes.description: Ericsson's Canadian business: 3,100+ staff with R&D centres and offices in Ottawa, Montreal and the Toronto area (Mississauga). Investing over CAD 630M in Canadian R&D under a five-year Strategic Innovation Fund agreement (Nov 2024) covering 5G Advanced, 6G, AI, Cloud RAN and quantum. Multi-year 6G/AI partnership with the University of Toronto (Feb 2026) and the AWIN mission-critical wireless network with the Government of Canada (May 2026).

nodes.name: Nokia Canada Ottawa campus
nodes.address: 600 March Road, Kanata North, Ottawa, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Nokia's main Canadian R&D site in the Kanata North tech park. Building a new 750,000 sq ft innovation campus (groundbreaking Nov 2025) for AI-powered networks, data centre networking, quantum-safe infrastructure, optics, IP routing and 6G. About 1,900 R&D staff in Ottawa, 2,500+ in Canada. Backed by the federal Strategic Innovation Fund.

nodes.name: Kanata North Business Association (Kanata North Tech Park)
nodes.address: Kanata North Tech Park, Ottawa, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Business association for Kanata North, Canada's largest technology park (800+ companies), home to Nokia and Ericsson's Ottawa R&D sites. Designated a Special Economic District in 2021.

nodes.name: National Research Council Canada (NRC)
nodes.description: Canada's national research organisation. Its High-throughput and Secure Networks (HTSN) Challenge program (2019 to 2026) developed next-generation network technology, including terahertz receivers for 6G, mmWave reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, photonics and optical satellite links.

nodes.name: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
nodes.description: Federal department for innovation, telecoms and spectrum. Funds Ericsson's and Nokia's Canadian R&D through the Strategic Innovation Fund and endorsed the international 6G principles in 2024.

nodes.name: Carleton University
nodes.address: 1125 Colonel By Drive, Ottawa, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Ottawa research university. Its Non-Terrestrial Networks Lab (Carleton-NTN), led by Halim Yanikomeroglu, works on 6G satellite, high-altitude platform and AI-enabled mega-constellation networks, and hosts industry partners including Ericsson.

nodes.name: University of Ottawa
nodes.address: 75 Laurier Ave E, Ottawa, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Ottawa research university. Home of the NETCORE lab (AI-enabled next-generation wireless) with partners including Ericsson, Nokia and Ciena, and NRC partner on terahertz receivers for 6G. Also runs a Kanata North campus.

nodes.name: University of Toronto
nodes.address: 10 King's College Road, Toronto, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Toronto research university. Its ECE Communications Group works on machine learning for wireless, joint sensing and communications, and massive random access. Signed a multi-year AI and next-generation mobile partnership with Ericsson in February 2026.

nodes.name: University of Waterloo
nodes.address: 200 University Ave W, Waterloo, ON, Canada
nodes.description: Research university in the Toronto–Waterloo corridor. Its Broadband Communications Research (BBCR) Lab works on 6G network architecture, intelligent network management, satellite networks and wireless security; the university is also a major quantum research centre.

nodes.name: McGill University
nodes.address: 817 Sherbrooke St W, Montreal, QC, Canada
nodes.description: Montreal research university with long-standing broadband wireless research, including dense and ultra-dense 5G-and-beyond access networks.

nodes.name: Polytechnique Montréal (Poly-Grames)
nodes.address: 2500 Chemin de Polytechnique, Montreal, QC, Canada
nodes.description: Engineering school whose Poly-Grames research centre (microwaves and space electronics) works on millimetre-wave and terahertz circuits, antennas and transceivers for 6G communication and sensing.

nodes.name: École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS)
nodes.address: 1100 Notre-Dame St W, Montreal, QC, Canada
nodes.description: Montreal engineering school. Home of Georges Kaddoum's research on 6G IoT networks and wireless security, and the Resilient Machine Learning Institute (ReMI) for tactical wireless networks.

nodes.role: President, Ericsson Canada

nodes.description: Head of Ericsson's Ottawa R&D site, taking over from Marcos Cavaletti in 2026, and Chief Technology Officer of Ericsson Canada. 20+ years in R&D, sales, strategy and product management across North America, Asia and Europe. BEng and MEng, McGill; MBA, Maastricht.

nodes.name: Prasad Garigipati
nodes.role: Head of Ericsson AI Hub Canada (Montreal)
nodes.description: Heads Ericsson's AI Hub Canada in Montreal. Visited Carleton's Non-Terrestrial Networks Lab with the Ottawa leadership team in July 2026.

nodes.name: Kelly Daize

nodes.description: Executive Director of the Kanata North Business Association since June 2024. Former Invest Ottawa executive and co-founder of CENGN, Canada's centre of excellence in next-generation networks.

nodes.name: Angela Gamouras
nodes.role: Research Officer, NRC Quantum and Nanotechnologies Research Centre
nodes.description: NRC researcher leading terahertz receiver work for 6G under the High-throughput and Secure Networks Challenge program, with the University of Ottawa and OZ Optics.

nodes.name: Halim Yanikomeroglu
nodes.role: Chancellor's Professor, Systems and Computer Engineering, Carleton University
nodes.description: Chancellor's Professor at Carleton and lead of the Carleton Non-Terrestrial Networks Lab, working on 6G satellite, high-altitude platform and AI-enabled mega-constellation networks. 2026 IEEE Canada R.A. Fessenden Award for pioneering 4G/5G/6G research. Prominent voice on Canada's 6G strategy.

nodes.name: Melike Erol-Kantarci
nodes.role: Professor and Canada Research Chair, University of Ottawa; Strategic Product Manager, AI RAN, Ericsson
nodes.description: Full Professor and Canada Research Chair (Tier 2) in AI-Enabled Next-Generation Wireless Networks at the University of Ottawa, where she leads the NETCORE lab. Also Strategic Product Manager for AI in RAN at Ericsson. IEEE Fellow.

nodes.name: Wei Yu
nodes.role: Professor and Canada Research Chair (Tier 1), ECE, University of Toronto
nodes.description: Professor and Tier 1 Canada Research Chair in Information Theory and Wireless Communications at the University of Toronto. Lab works on machine learning for wireless, joint sensing and communications, massive random access and 5G/6G cellular networks.

nodes.name: Weihua Zhuang
nodes.role: University Professor and Canada Research Chair (Tier 1), ECE, University of Waterloo
nodes.description: University Professor and Tier 1 Canada Research Chair in wireless communication networks at Waterloo's BBCR Lab. Works on network architectures and intelligent network management for 6G.

nodes.name: Xuemin (Sherman) Shen
nodes.role: University Professor Emeritus and Adjunct Professor, ECE, University of Waterloo
nodes.description: Wireless networking pioneer at Waterloo's BBCR Lab, retired in 2026 and now University Professor Emeritus and Adjunct Professor. Past President of the IEEE Communications Society. 2026 IEEE Canada A.G.L. McNaughton Award.

nodes.name: Tho Le-Ngoc
nodes.role: Professor, ECE, McGill University
nodes.description: McGill professor working on broadband wireless access, transmission and resource allocation for dense 5G-and-beyond networks. Fellow of IEEE, the Royal Society of Canada and the Canadian Academy of Engineering.

nodes.name: Ke Wu
nodes.role: Professor, Electrical Engineering, Polytechnique Montréal (Poly-Grames)
nodes.description: Professor at Polytechnique Montréal's Poly-Grames centre, leading research on millimetre-wave and terahertz circuits, waveguides and large-array front-ends for 6G communication and sensing. IEEE Fellow.

nodes.name: Georges Kaddoum
nodes.role: Professor and Canada Research Chair, ÉTS Montréal
nodes.description: Professor at ÉTS and Canada Research Chair in Unlocking the Power of IoT 6G-Networks. Co-founded the Resilient Machine Learning Institute (ReMI) for tactical wireless networks and worked with Ericsson Canada on security for NFV-based 5G networks.

nodes.name: Pi-Radio
nodes.description: NYU WIRELESS spin-off, supported by NYU Tandon's Center for Advanced Technology in Telecommunications, making software-defined radios for frequencies above 6 GHz: 140 GHz arrays and wideband FR3 (6 to 24 GHz) kits for upper mid-band 6G research. Partner on NTIA Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund grants with NYU Tandon.

nodes.name: Thomas L. Marzetta
nodes.role: Distinguished Industry Professor, ECE, NYU Tandon; NYU WIRELESS
nodes.description: Distinguished Industry Professor at NYU Tandon and originator of Massive MIMO. Previously Director of NYU WIRELESS. Works on mmWave and terahertz communications and super-directive wireless power transfer. NYU WIRELESS's January 2026 workshop marked twenty years of Massive MIMO.

nodes.name: Marwa Chafii
nodes.role: Associate Professor, ECE, NYU; NYU WIRELESS
nodes.description: Associate Professor leading NYU WIRELESS work on integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) for 6G: AI-based ISAC, channel modelling for sensing, multi-band ISAC in the upper mid-band, and waveform design. Honoured by Women in 6G.

nodes.name: Hamed Rahmani
nodes.role: Assistant Professor, ECE, NYU Tandon; RAISE Lab
nodes.description: Leads the Research in Advanced Integrated Systems and Electronics (RAISE) Lab, designing mmWave and sub-THz circuits, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces and near-field sub-THz networks. Co-leads the RFIC work on the $10M NTIA-funded SALSA upper mid-band project.

nodes.name: Shivendra Panwar
nodes.role: Professor, ECE, NYU Tandon; Director, Center for Advanced Technology in Telecommunications (CATT)
nodes.description: Director of NYU Tandon's Center for Advanced Technology in Telecommunications (CATT) for 30 years and NYU WIRELESS faculty member. Works on network design, low-latency and ultra-reliable wireless, and the COSMOS city-scale testbed. IEEE ComSoc Distinguished Lecturer; Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors.

nodes.name: Davood Shahrjerdi
nodes.role: Professor, ECE, NYU Tandon; Faculty Director, NYU Nanofabrication Cleanroom
nodes.description: Directs the NYU Nanofab cleanroom and is co-PI of the NSF-funded THz Measurement Facility at NYU WIRELESS, working on new electronic materials and devices for high-frequency wireless.

nodes.name: Michael E. Knox
nodes.role: Industry Professor, ECE, NYU Tandon
nodes.description: Industry Professor and senior personnel on the NYU WIRELESS THz Measurement Facility. Leads the VIP-300X Wireless 6G undergraduate course using the THz lab.

nodes.name: Sundar Aditya
nodes.role: Researcher, NYU WIRELESS
nodes.description: NYU WIRELESS researcher working on integrated sensing and communications, wideband localisation, radar and terahertz communications. Formerly a postdoc with Sundeep Rangan.

nodes.description: Associate Director of NYU WIRELESS. Leads work on 5G-connected wearables and sensory augmentation for people with blindness and low vision.

nodes.role: Researcher, Pi-Radio
nodes.description: Pi-Radio researcher and former NYU WIRELESS postdoc. Built the wideband FR3 (6 to 24 GHz) software-defined radio used for upper mid-band 6G experiments under NTIA funding.

nodes.name: Mike Zappe
nodes.role: Engineer, Pi-Radio
nodes.description: Pi-Radio engineer on the NTIA-funded FR3 software-defined radio for upper mid-band 6G experiments.

nodes.name: Open6G (Northeastern University)

nodes.description: Northeastern's federal-industry-university 6G hub, run by the Institute for Intelligent Networked Systems (INSI, formerly the Institute for the Wireless Internet of Things). Works on Open RAN, AI/ML network control, spectrum sharing and digital twins. Hosts the Colosseum emulator, the O-RAN Alliance-approved North American OTIC in the Boston Area, and an AI-RAN Alliance-endorsed lab. Funded by an OUSD(R&E) FutureG anchor award. Launched Open6G+AI in February 2026.

nodes.name: Michele Polese
nodes.role: Research Associate Professor, ECE; Technical Director, Institute for Intelligent Networked Systems, Northeastern
nodes.description: Technical Director of Northeastern's Institute for Intelligent Networked Systems and principal investigator of Open6G+AI, the open-source AI-RAN ecosystem launched in 2026. Leads the O-RAN digital twin work on Colosseum and a $2M Wireless Innovation Fund project (AutoRAN). Elected to an AI-RAN Alliance working group role.

nodes.name: Salvatore D'Oro
nodes.role: Associate Research Professor, ECE, Northeastern University
nodes.description: Open RAN and AI-for-RAN researcher at INSI. Co-inventor on patents for Open RAN adapters, intelligence in the RAN and software-defined cellular networks. Works on the Colosseum digital twin and AI-automated private 5G.

nodes.name: Leonardo Bonati
nodes.role: Associate Research Scientist, ECE, Northeastern University
nodes.description: INSI researcher building Open6G's Open RAN testbeds, OpenRAN Gym and the Colosseum O-RAN digital twin. Co-inventor on Open RAN and private 5G patents.

nodes.name: Francesco Restuccia
nodes.role: Assistant Professor, ECE, Northeastern University
nodes.description: Works on AI-driven wireless systems for 5G and 6G, including spectrum and multi-band MIMO. Holds an ONR Young Investigator award on 6G spectrum dominance and a 2025 DARPA Young Faculty Award. 2026 IEEE INFOCOM Best Paper Award.

nodes.name: Stefano Basagni
nodes.role: Professor, ECE; Associate Dean of the Global Engineering Campus, Northeastern University
nodes.description: Core faculty of Northeastern's wireless institute and part of the Colosseum leadership team. Co-author of the work turning Colosseum into a digital twin for 6G research.

nodes.name: Northeastern University London (INSI London hub)
nodes.address: One Portsoken, Portsoken Street, London E1 8BT, UK
nodes.description: London hub of Northeastern's Institute for Intelligent Networked Systems, launched January 2026 and its first research office outside the US. Works on next-generation connectivity, AI for wireless and brain-inspired communications for 6G (NeuroComm), networked machine learning (FreeML) and reliable AI for wireless (CONTRACT). Funders include EPSRC, ERC, Horizon Europe, Innovate UK and ARIA.

nodes.name: Osvaldo Simeone
nodes.role: Professor of Information Engineering; Co-Director, Intelligent Networked Systems Institute, Northeastern University London
nodes.description: Co-directs INSI at Northeastern University London. Leads the FreeML and CONTRACT projects on networked and reliable machine learning for wireless, and co-leads NeuroComm on brain-inspired communications for 6G. Visiting Professor at Aalborg University.

nodes.name: Bipin Rajendran
nodes.role: Professor of Intelligent Computing Systems, Intelligent Networked Systems Institute, Northeastern University London
nodes.description: Professor at the INSI London hub working on neuromorphic and brain-inspired computing hardware. Co-leads NeuroComm with Osvaldo Simeone on brain-inspired wireless communications for 6G and beyond.

nodes.name: 6G@UT Research Center
nodes.address: Engineering Education and Research Center, 2501 Speedway, Austin, TX 78712

Works on machine learning for wireless, sensing and localisation, and network intelligence. Founding affiliates: Samsung, AT&T, NVIDIA, Qualcomm and InterDigital; Ericsson joined in 2022.

nodes.name: Ericsson Austin R&D Center
nodes.description: Ericsson's Austin R&D Center, opened in 2017 with 250+ staff. Teams in semiconductor (ASIC), software and AI design the silicon and hardware for Ericsson radio networks, and are developing next-generation architectures for 6G.

nodes.name: Samsung Research America (Plano, TX)
nodes.description: Samsung Research America's Plano site, home of its Standards and Mobility Innovation (SMI) lab: 5G/6G research, prototyping and 3GPP standards work, including AI-native wireless and sensing.

nodes.name: Verizon 6G Innovation Forum
nodes.description: Verizon-led consortium on 6G use cases and research. Samsung is a founding member. In July 2026 Verizon and Samsung ran an AI-powered ISAC (integrated sensing and communication) crowd-sensing field trial over virtualised RAN at a soccer fan event in Dallas.

nodes.name: Georgia Tech (Center for Wireless Intelligence)
nodes.address: Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA 30332
nodes.description: Georgia Tech's Center for Wireless Intelligence (CWI), launched in 2025, runs an outdoor urban wireless testbed for 6G research, including integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and supports research through prototyping to domestic production.

nodes.name: Princeton University (NextG Initiative)
nodes.description: Princeton's NextG Initiative, formed in 2023, links faculty and a corporate affiliates programme on wireless, terahertz integrated circuits, networking and cloud. Affiliates include Samsung Research America, Ericsson, Intel, MediaTek, Nokia Bell Labs, Qualcomm and Vodafone.

nodes.name: Purdue University (NextG Center)
nodes.description: Purdue's NextG Center for Communications and Sensing (XGC) works on massive and cell-free MIMO, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, machine learning for wireless, and rural access. Purdue Research Foundation's Lab to Life zone in the Discovery Park District is a 6G deployment testbed.

nodes.name: Northwestern University
nodes.description: Northwestern's ECE department works on spectrum management and wireless networking for NextG. Its faculty take part in the NSF SpectrumX centre, with Michael Honig as SpectrumX research director.

nodes.name: CableLabs
nodes.description: Cable industry R&D consortium. Its Advanced Wireless Lab works on 5G/6G architecture, mobile and cable convergence, and contributes to 3GPP 6G study work so broadband-centric deployment models are reflected in the 6G standard.

nodes.name: Idaho National Laboratory (INL)
nodes.address: 1955 N Fremont Ave, Idaho Falls, ID 83415
nodes.description: DOE national laboratory. Industry partners include Nokia, Qualcomm, Cisco, Verizon and InterDigital.

nodes.role: Distinguished Wireless Communications Researcher, Idaho National Laboratory
nodes.description: INL researcher developing adaptive wireless spectrum technologies, including work with NIST for NTIA.

nodes.name: INATEL (National Institute of Telecommunications)
nodes.address: Av. João de Camargo 510, Santa Rita do Sapucaí, MG 37540-000, Brazil
nodes.description: Brazil's National Institute of Telecommunications in Santa Rita do Sapucaí, Minas Gerais ('Electronics Valley'). Executes the Brasil 6G project and hosts xGMobile, the Embrapii-Inatel Competence Center for 5G and 6G Networks, and the Radiocommunications Reference Center (CRR). Use cases include agribusiness, mining and environmental monitoring. Partner of the University of Oulu's 6G Flagship since 2017.

nodes.name: Brasil 6G Project
nodes.description: National 6G research programme created by Brazil's Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI) as a Priority IT Programme (PPI). Coordinated by RNP and executed by INATEL with CPQD and universities including Unicamp, UFRJ, UFC, UFPA, UFSC, UFU, UFG and Unisinos. Entered its third phase (prototypes and remote-access testing) in the second half of 2024.

nodes.name: RNP (National Education and Research Network)
nodes.description: Brazil's National Education and Research Network. Coordinates the Brasil 6G programme and the OpenRAN@Brasil and 5G-in-a-box Priority IT projects for MCTI.

nodes.name: MCTI (Brazil Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation)
nodes.description: Brazilian federal ministry that created and funds the Brasil 6G programme and OpenRAN@Brasil through its Priority IT Programmes.

nodes.name: CPQD (Telecommunications Research and Development Center)
nodes.address: Rua Dr. Ricardo Benetton Martins 1000, Campinas, SP, Brazil
nodes.description: Latin America's largest ICT R&D centre and an independent, government-affiliated body. Partner in Brasil 6G and OpenRAN@Brasil, and host of the Embrapii CPQD Open RAN Competence Center, Latin America's first accredited Open RAN test and integration centre (OTIC). Manages R$104M of Funttel funds for 6G and AI (2026 to 2028).

nodes.name: Unicamp (SMARTNESS Research Center)
nodes.address: FEEC, Universidade Estadual de Campinas, Campinas, SP, Brazil
nodes.description: State University of Campinas. Hosts SMARTNESS (Smart Networks and Services for 2030), a FAPESP Engineering Research Center with Ericsson (2023 to 2033) working on cognitive, autonomous 5G/6G networks and cloud-edge services. Also a Brasil 6G partner.

nodes.name: FAPESP (São Paulo Research Foundation)
nodes.description: São Paulo State research funding agency. Co-funds the SMARTNESS 5G/6G Engineering Research Center at Unicamp with Ericsson.

nodes.name: Ericsson Brazil R&D Center (Indaiatuba)
nodes.description: Ericsson's research, development and innovation centre in Indaiatuba near Campinas, home of Ericsson Research Brazil and the 5G Open Innovation Center (2025). Works closely with the SMARTNESS centre at Unicamp on autonomous networks and 6G.

nodes.name: Federal University of Pará (UFPA)
nodes.description: Federal university in Belém. Partner in Brasil 6G and OpenRAN@Brasil.

nodes.name: Federal University of Ceará (UFC)
nodes.description: Federal university in Fortaleza. Partner in the Brasil 6G project.

nodes.name: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)
nodes.description: Federal university in Rio de Janeiro. Partner in Brasil 6G and OpenRAN@Brasil.

nodes.name: Federal University of Uberlândia (UFU)

nodes.description: Chile's state economic development agency. Its Technological Capabilities division backs the Subtel and OnLab industrial 5G/6G pilot programme.

nodes.name: University of Manitoba
nodes.address: 66 Chancellors Circle, Winnipeg, MB R3T 2N2, Canada
nodes.description: Winnipeg university. Partner with Ericsson, Concordia and Waterloo on AI-based security for 5G and future 6G networks under the National Cybersecurity Consortium.

nodes.name: University of British Columbia (UBC)
nodes.address: 2329 West Mall, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z4, Canada
nodes.description: Vancouver university. Canada's first 5G smart campus (with Rogers) and a living lab for next-generation wireless. Its ICICS institute and Arctic research programme work on secure 5G/6G communications, sensing and AI for harsh Arctic conditions and defence applications.

nodes.name: National Cybersecurity Consortium (NCC)
nodes.description: Leads the Government of Canada's Cyber Security Innovation Network (up to CAD 80M). Funds the Ericsson, Concordia, Manitoba and Waterloo project on AI-based security for 5G and future 6G networks.

nodes.name: Rogers Communications

nodes.name: Yonsei University (AI-RAN research)

nodes.description: Seoul university leading Korea's AI-RAN joint research: signed an AI-RAN MOU with NVIDIA, Samsung Electronics, SK Telecom, KT, LG Uplus and ETRI at APEC Summit Korea 2025. Runs an NVIDIA GPU-based AI-RAN test network and hosts the 6G Open Hub (with NI).

nodes.name: Korea University
nodes.address: Korea University, Anam-dong, Seoul, South Korea

nodes.name: KAIST (LG-KAIST 6G Research Center)
nodes.description: Daejeon research university. Hosts the LG-KAIST 6G Research Center (2019), Korea's first industry-academic 6G centre, which developed a 27 GHz-bandwidth terahertz beamforming system (143 to 170 GHz) with KRISS and Keysight. Also works on wireless power transfer.

nodes.description: Korea's national measurement institute. Partner with LG Electronics and KAIST on 6G terahertz technology development, verification and test infrastructure (MOU 2020).

nodes.description: Led the LG-KAIST 6G Research Center from its launch in 2019.
